ops.title: just redeploy does in-place state-preserving redeploys; hermes \"must disk-replace\" was folklore, in-guest switch is the path
ops.body:
Added `just redeploy [host|metal|hermes|bluebubbles|all]` (`scripts/redeploy.sh`) on 2026-06-24:
unattended, state-preserving, zero-human-input redeploy of an already-bootstrapped fleet for
"we added a dep/package/plugin". metal = in-guest `darwin-rebuild switch` (new `metal-redeploy`
helper sourcing the GitHub token in-guest from `/run/secrets/vault/static-keys`); hermes =
in-guest `nixos-rebuild switch --flake /var/lib/yclaw-repo#hermes` (new ro `repo` virtiofs share,
dry-activate-gated, plain git-flake ref NOT `path:` which would leak gitignored `.build`/secrets
into the world-readable store); bluebubbles = new `reconfigure` subcommand, never touches the
disk. The disk-replace fallback (`scripts/deploy-vm.sh`, reserved for kernel/initrd/bootloader
changes) auto-RE-MINTS a fresh ephemeral authkey via `scripts/remint-hermes-authkey.sh` before the
clonefile. CORRECTION (2026-06-27): an earlier attempt to persist `/var/lib/tailscale` to a host
share was REMOVED — hermes is an EPHEMERAL tailnet node (reaped on disconnect), so the node key
can't survive a disk-replace, AND a mount over `/var/lib/tailscale` collides with the tailscale
module's `StateDirectory=tailscale` and makes tailscaled FAIL to start. See [[metal-reboot-survival]]
sibling finding; in-guest switch never disconnects hermes so it keeps its node naturally.

**Why:** the repo previously had NO clean redeploy path and DEPLOY.md claimed hermes *must*
disk-replace because `nixos-rebuild switch` "hits a virtiofs remount quirk."

**How to apply:** the quirk is **real but CONDITIONAL** — not folklore, but also not "switch always
breaks." Apple virtiofs can't re-enumerate a tag once unmounted mid-session (`virtio-fs: tag not
found`, observed 2026-06-18, see [[hermes-deploy-and-bluebubbles-addressing]]), so switch breaks ONLY
when it would start/stop/restart a virtiofs mount; `switch-to-configuration` leaves byte-identical
mounts untouched, so a code-only deploy is safe. `scripts/redeploy.sh` gates on `nixos-rebuild
dry-activate` and routes any mount-touching deploy to the disk-replace fallback. Lesson: the old
DEPLOY.md one-liner OVERstated it (always-breaks); my first pass UNDERstated it (folklore) by missing
the 2026-06-18 observation — check a claim AND your refutation against ALL evidence (git-history +
first-principles + dry-activate + existing memories + an outside check). metal is immune (its virtiofs
shares are tart auto-mounts, not nix-managed units). Full rationale: repo cc-notes doc (trigger:
redeploy pipeline). Also fixed: cli-proxy OAuth tokens wrote to a non-existent `state` share. Related:
[[deploy-pipeline-fixes-2026-06]], [[security-hardening-2026-06]].
